chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying while he was in prostration: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You exchange my bad deeds for good ones, and reckon me with an easy reckoning.'

Then he said during the second (prostration): 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You suffice me with the provisions of the world and every terror before Paradise.'

And he said during the third: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have forgiven me the many sins and the few, and accepted from me my slight deeds.'

Then he said during the fourth: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have brought me into Paradise and made me from its dwellers, and since You have saved me from the blasts of the Fire by Your mercy. And may Allah bless Muhammad and his family.'

key_terms.بَدَّلْتَ سَيِّئَاتِي حَسَنَاتٍ: Exchange my bad deeds for good ones
key_terms.حَقِّ حَبِيبِكَ: The right of Your beloved (referring to Prophet Muhammad)
key_terms.حِسَاباً يَسِيراً: An easy reckoning (on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications recited during the four prostrations in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia practice of invoking the 'Haqq' (right/authority) of the Prophet Muhammad as a means of intercession during the intimate moments of prostration. It reflects the theological concept of *Tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, where the supplicant asks Allah to transform sins into good deeds and grant ease in the Hereafter based on the Prophet's merit. The structure emphasizes a progressive spiritual journey from forgiveness to ultimate salvation, rooted in divine mercy.
